_comment: Site-shaped rule. The prefilter narrows a TypeScript/JavaScript tree to conditions built from several boolean operands; the model judges whether the condition encodes a domain concept that deserves a name. Unlike `swallowed-error`, this pattern is COMMON — which is what makes it usable as a calibration control.
title: A compound condition encodes a domain rule that has no name and cannot be tested on its own
match: The site is a condition (an `if`/`while` test, a ternary test, a filter/guard callback, or an early-return test) that combines THREE OR MORE operands, or mixes `&&` with `||`, AND the combination expresses a single domain idea — eligibility, validity, readiness, permission, staleness — that appears nowhere as a name in the surrounding lines you were given. The test is whether a reader must mentally evaluate the operators to learn what the condition MEANS: if the meaning is only recoverable by decoding, the concept is unnamed. A condition inside a function can only be exercised by calling that function, so the more setup the enclosing function needs — I/O, many parameters, mocked collaborators — the more this condition is effectively untested logic, and the stronger the finding.
no_match: The condition is a presence or null guard (`if (!x) return`, `x && x.y && x.y.z`). It is a fallback chain choosing a default (`a || b || 'default'`), which selects a value rather than expressing a rule. Its operands are ALREADY named predicates or well-named booleans (`isActive(u) && hasQuota(u)`) — the concept is named, only combined. The condition is already assigned to a named local or function and the site merely uses it (`const isEligible = ...; if (isEligible)`) — that is the FIXED form of this pattern, never a finding. It is a TypeScript narrowing chain the compiler requires inline. It is arithmetic or a range comparison whose meaning is self-evident. Test code, generated code, or a `.d.ts`. The condition already lives in its own small predicate function or pure helper — that is the fixed form.
evidence: The condition, copied verbatim from its opening operand to its last. `line` is where the condition begins.
why_hint: Name the domain concept the condition encodes, then PROPOSE an extracted predicate in backticks as a SIGNATURE, not just a name — camelCase, prefixed `is`/`has`/`can`/`should`, returning a boolean, and taking ONLY the values the condition actually reads rather than a whole object (prefer `isRenewalEligible({status, daysOverdue, balance})` over `isRenewalEligible(subscription)`, because the narrower signature is what makes it testable without fixtures). State in one clause what a reader must currently decode, and in one clause what it would take to test this condition TODAY — what the enclosing function requires in order to be called at all. Do not speculate about callers or duplicates outside the surrounding lines you were given; if you believe the same condition appears elsewhere, say 'possible duplicate not visible in the surrounding lines you were given'.
